transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having these nagging thoughts that I might’ve forgotten something important. Like, I’ll worry I left my aunt’s medicine out the wrong way, or that I didn’t set up my classroom materials safely enough.

I know that probably sounds a little silly, because usually I’m pretty responsible and I’m fairly sure I handled it, but the doubt just keeps popping back into my head anyway. I thought maybe it would be good to talk to someone about it.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over, like checking, counting, or trying to neutralize the thoughts in some way?

Um… yes, a little. I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s extreme or anything, but before I leave the house or my classroom, I do tend to go back over the same things a few times.

Like I’ll check the pill organizer, or the stove, or make sure my lesson plans and materials are set the way they should be. And sometimes I’ll sort of replay in my head what I did, just to be sure. Usually after I do that enough, I feel calm enough to leave, but… it can make me run late sometimes. I know that’s probably not ideal.
Do these thoughts and the need to check things over and over cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your day-to-day life, like taking up a lot of time or affecting your work or relationships?

I mean… I’m still managing everything, mostly. I get to work, I take care of my family responsibilities, so I don’t want to make it sound like my life is falling apart or anything.

But it does slow me down. Mornings take longer than they should, and sometimes I get to school feeling rushed, like I’m already behind before the day even starts. And things that used to feel kind of calming, like getting my lessons ready or journaling in the evening, don’t feel as smooth or restorative lately.

So… I guess it interferes some. Not terribly, but enough that I’m noticing it. Does that make sense?
Do you ever have thoughts that pop into your mind that you don’t want or welcome, that cause you anxiety or discomfort?

Yes… I think that’s a fair way to put it. It’s not like I want to be thinking about these things, and I know most of the time I probably did everything correctly.

But the thought will pop in anyway, like, “What if I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong?” or “What if something in my classroom wasn’t set up safely?” And then I feel this uncomfortable doubt, even if part of me knows it’s probably okay. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but yes, that does happen.
When you have those unwanted thoughts, do you feel driven to perform certain mental or physical actions to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think I do. I don’t know if it’s, like, a huge thing, but when that doubt pops up, I feel like I need to check just one more time.

Before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back over the same things a few times — the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans or materials — just to make sure I didn’t miss anything. And sometimes I sort of replay what I did in my head, quietly, until I feel calm enough to move on.

I know it probably sounds unnecessary, and I can usually stop eventually, but it does make me late sometimes.
Do you find that your checking behaviors or mental rituals take up more than an hour of your day in total?

I don’t think it’s usually more than an hour, no… at least, I hope not. It’s more like little chunks that add up, especially when I’m leaving the house or leaving my classroom.

I’ll check the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans or materials, and sometimes I’ll replay what I did in my head until I feel settled enough to go. It can make me run late sometimes, but I don’t think it takes over the whole day. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
Have these thoughts or the need to check things ever caused problems with your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still doing what I need to do. I get to work, I take care of family things, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But my mornings do take longer than they should, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or kind of behind before the day has even started. And with lesson prep, I notice it doesn’t feel as smooth as it used to. Even my journaling at night, which used to feel calming, can feel less restorative now.

So… yes, I guess it has affected things some, just not in a way where everything is falling apart. Does that make sense?
Can you think of a time when you checked something even though you knew, logically, that it was already safe or taken care of?

Yes… I can think of that. Like, I’ll know I already put my pills in the organizer, or I’ll remember turning the stove off, but then right before I leave I get this little doubt and I go back anyway.

At school it can be the same with my lesson plans or materials — I know I checked them, but I’ll look again, or kind of replay in my head what I did step by step until I feel settled.

I know logically it’s probably fine, and I’m not trying to be difficult or anything… it just feels like I can’t quite leave it alone until I feel calm enough. And sometimes that’s what makes me run late.
Have these thoughts or behaviors ever made it hard for you to connect with others, enjoy activities, or perform at your best at work, even if you’re still managing your responsibilities?

Yes… I think so, but maybe in a mild way? I don’t want to overstate it because I am still getting through work and family things.

But my mornings definitely take longer than they probably should, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or like I’m behind before the day even starts. And with lesson prep, I don’t feel as smooth or confident getting things together as I used to.

Even my evening journaling, which used to help me unwind, doesn’t feel quite as restorative lately. So… yes, it has affected things some, just not to the point where I’m not functioning. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had unwanted thoughts about germs, dirt, or contamination, or felt the need to wash or clean things repeatedly because of those thoughts?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I like things to be clean, especially at school with kids and everything, but I don’t think I have unwanted thoughts about germs or dirt in that way.

I don’t usually feel like I have to wash or clean something over and over to feel okay. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever had thoughts that something bad might happen if things aren’t done in a specific way, or if things don’t feel ‘just right,’ even if you know it’s probably irrational?

Yes… I think that’s pretty close, actually. I wouldn’t say I believe something terrible will definitely happen, but I get these nagging thoughts that maybe I forgot something important.

Like with my aunt’s medicine, I’ll worry I left it out wrong or didn’t handle it the way I should have. Or at school, I’ll start wondering if I set up the classroom materials safely enough. Even when I can tell myself, “No, you probably did that,” the doubt kind of pops back in anyway.

It feels a little embarrassing to say, because I know it’s probably irrational… but it’s like I need it to feel settled or right before I can move on. Does that make sense?
